name: Febuxostat
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Febuxostat needs no dose change in mild to moderate kidney impairment. In severe impairment the US label limits the dose to 40 mg once daily, and it has not been studied in people on dialysis.

bands.recommendation: No dose adjustment (label: mild impairment, CrCl 30 to 89 mL/min, needs none).
Not studied (PK study enrolled CrCl 10 to 29 mL/min). Insufficient data: use with specialist input.

hd.text: Not studied in end-stage renal impairment on dialysis (label). Insufficient data: use with specialist input.

pd.text: Not studied (label). Insufficient data: use with specialist input.

crrt.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: use with specialist input.

monitoring: Serum urate; liver tests per label. The label carries a boxed warning on cardiovascular death.

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and effectiveness not established in pediatric patients (label).

renal.recommendation: Not established in children; do not use outside specialist care.

pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: Label severe band is CrCl 15–29; the PK study included CrCl 10–29. Nothing in the label covers CrCl <15 or dialysis.
Consider whether the boxed cardiovascular-death warning belongs in the kidney panel or only in the label accordion.
pediatric: Not established in children; no extrapolation offered.
